PLOT 4-C — TIDAL ZONE A
SAMPLING WINDOW 04/22
SALT MARSH
CARDIGAN BAY
FIELD REPORT
Three years on, the Cardigan Bay saltmarsh is holding sediment faster than projected.

Our hydrology contractor wrapped the third annual sediment survey last week. The averaged accretion rate across the four monitored plots is now 8.2 mm/year — well above the 5.5 mm/year baseline we used when modelling site viability in 2022.

It's a modest but meaningful proof point: the dyke breach we funded with the Llanrhystud parish is, by every measurable, doing what it was supposed to do.

FIELD REPORT
BEAVER DAM ANALOGUES
Beaver dam analogues at Glen Lyon: first measurable channel widening.

Year three reading across the eight BDA structures shows mean wetted width up 41% and a measurable drop in summer water temperatures. Field crew notes attached. Photographs available on request.

CARBON LEDGER
From the Carpentaria Floor: thirty hectares of old growth burnt and under perpetual protection.

This quarter we closed the long-pending purchase of a 30-ha private parcel adjoining the Mitchell River wilderness. It is the second tranche of a slow consolidation: small private holdings, no fanfare, no eviction.

OP-ED
Year-three survival audit, Loch Awe planting: 75.4% across 144,000 stems.

A statistically meaningful sample of the September 2022 plantings was re-walked over the winter. We expected losses to be high in the rougher north-facing slopes; they came in lower than feared.

WETLANDS
Peat re-wetting at Border Mire: water table holding within 6 cm of surface for 218 of the last 220 monitored days.

Sphagnum recolonisation is visibly underway in the cleared drains. We have switched to monthly LIDAR overflights and an open data feed for the public-interest research community.
